## 26. `[settings.rent]` — the engine charges the money, so do not author a canvas that does

The recurring-demand system is real, it is wired end to end, and it **takes the money**. Read this
before writing a settle-up scene. **In one line: the engine arms the bill at 00:00 on the due day and
takes it on her next move; authored scenes sit beside the payment, never on it.**

```toml
[settings.rent]
enabled          = true
due_day          = "Friday"          # weekday names only — VALID_DAYS, template_import.py:6252
collector_npc    = "npc_collector"   # must exist in [[npcs]]
start_after_flag = "first_shift_done"
stages      = [ { amount = 100, after_total_paid = 0 }, { amount = 150, after_total_paid = 300 } ]
stage_lines = [ "…", "…" ]           # what the collector says when stages[i] takes over
on_short    = "carry"                # a short week is owed next week; no eviction, no game over
currency_symbol  = "$"               # rent pages only — eight other money prints hardcode "$" (§33)

[settings.rent.text]                  # every beat of the pages is authored here
title = "…" · scene = "…" · greeting = "…" · paid_scene = "…" · paid_response = "…"
paid_closing = "…" · cant_pay = "…" · partial_pay = "…"
```

**How it fires — and the timing is the part authors get wrong.**

1. `advanceDay()` (`v2.py:6605`) sets `rent_state.is_due` when the day rolls over **to** `due_day`
   (at `:6431`).
   Days roll at midnight (`v2.py:6570-6573`), so the demand arms at **00:00 on the due day**, not at
   whatever hour the collector's schedule row says.
2. The next time the player lands on a `Location_*` passage or `Navigation`, they are intercepted
   into `RentDay` (`v2.py:18052-18061`). Never mid-canvas.
3. Paying runs `$player.core_traits.money -= _rent` and clears `is_due` (`v2.py:18846`). Verified
   live.
4. A short week with `on_short = "carry"` is paid as far as she can and the rest is owed next week
   (`setup.carryRent`, `v2.py:14169`); nothing ends.

**`start_after_flag` is what stops it being a scripted loss.** Until that flag is set the demand
never arms, so the flag belongs on the canvas that first gives her a way to earn.

> ⚠️ **DO NOT ALSO WRITE THE PAYMENT AS A CANVAS.** A hub rung that narrates the payment beside a
> working `[settings.rent]` gives the player two settle-ups; with no cost on the rung, one of them is
> free, and the free one is the one with the writing in it. If the engine takes the money, the authored scene beside it must be about something else.

**Money must be unclamped for this to work at all.** A demand above 100 against `clamp = true` money
(caps at 100) can never be paid in full — see §21.

- `setup.currentRent()` (`v2.py:14118`) is the amount at every read; the payment that moves the stage
  shows its line on the paid screen. `stages`, `stage_lines` and `on_short` are opt-in, emitted only
  when used. Keys: `template_import.py:522-531`.
- A stage with `after_total_paid = 0` is the starting rent: it is reached before any payment
  (`setup.recordRentPayment`, `v2.py:14124`), so its stage line never prints; put those words in the
  rent's own text (planned: an import warning for that shape).
- Carry sets the flag `rent_carried` and ignores `grace_periods` and `eviction_mode`. **No game over
  over rent** *(LO decided, D8d)*.
- **The old route**, without `on_short`: a fixed `amount`, a short week spends `grace_periods`, then
  the eviction branch — `eviction_mode = "flag_set"` sets `eviction_flag`; the default `"game_end"`
  ends the game.
- Old saves: `total_paid` and `owed` backfill to 0, so a save restarts at stage 1 owing nothing.

# These pages render on every Friday at every stage of Martin's arc, so nothing here claims a past
# or says whether he has touched her yet. The stage lines decide whether he counts it.
scene         = "It's Friday. Martin is at the head of the kitchen table in his suit, coffee at his elbow, the paper in one hand. In front of him is a clean square of table with nothing on it. That's where your envelope goes. Your mother is at the stove. Ethan is at the counter with his mug, waiting to see you do it."
greeting      = "\"Friday, Emma.\" He doesn't look up from the paper. He doesn't need to. You can feel him waiting for you, like a hand on the back of your neck."
paid_scene    = "You put the envelope down in the empty square. That's your week, folded in half. He slides it over with two fingers and it goes inside his jacket, against his chest. Then he looks up. He takes his time about it, from your face down and slowly back up, with your mother three feet away. Your face goes hot. So does the rest of you, and you hate that he can probably tell."
paid_response = "\"Good girl.\" He says it low, like it's only for you. Your mother smiles at the stove like she didn't hear it. Ethan heard it. He sets his mug down hard and looks at you like you just proved his point. You should hate hearing it. You don't, and that's worse."
paid_closing  = "Go to work."
cant_pay      = "You don't have it, so you put nothing down. The square in front of him stays empty. He lowers the paper and looks at you over it for a long time. Your mother stops stirring. Ethan stops chewing. \"Then it's owed,\" Martin says. \"Next Friday it's all of it, Emma. You'll find a way. Girls like you always do.\" You know exactly what he means. He knows you know."
partial_pay   = "The envelope is thin, and you both see it before it touches the table. He counts it in front of everyone, one bill at a time, while your mother pretends to read the cereal box. \"Short.\" He puts it away. \"The rest next week, Emma. I keep track of everything you owe me.\" He watches your mouth while he says it, and your knees go stupid."
